R6.1.response: We are grateful for the force of this comment. It prompted us to audit the corpus far more carefully than we had, and the reviewer's suspicion turned out to be better founded than we realized. Three findings are new in this revision, and all three support the reviewer's concern. First, the submitted results were produced by a stratified random split rather than the temporal split our manuscript described; under a chronological split macro F1 falls from 99.95% to 97.88%. We regret this error and have corrected it. Second, before deduplication, 15.5% of test rows under that stratified split have a feature-identical twin in the training partition, and a lookup table that learns nothing reaches 99.28% accuracy, so a large share of the headline figure was available to memorisation. Third, and most useful to others working with this corpus, 97.9% of benign flows occur in the final 30% of the capture, with a median position of 0.995, so a chronological split leaves only 582 benign flows for training against 30,432 at test. On the wider point, we would gently offer that a corpus whose limitations have been measured and published is more useful to the community than one whose limitations remain unexamined, and we hope these measurements contribute in that spirit. We have also followed the reviewer's instruction to validate more broadly, adding transfer across four attack vectors, a second capture day, InSDN and CIC-IDS2017, with confidence intervals, and we report the degradation observed rather than the best case.
R6.1.action: Added the protocol audit, duplicate and memorisation analysis, temporal-structure analysis, and cross-vector, cross-day and cross-dataset evaluation.
R6.1.location: Sec. VII-B, Sec. VII-C, Sec. VII-D, Sec. VII-J, Sec. VII-K, Sec. IX-D

R7.1.response: The reviewer is right that entropy features, a Random Forest and TreeSHAP are individually standard, and the revision no longer claims otherwise. What we argue is novel is the operational accounting around them, and the revision makes each element concrete and measurable rather than asserted. The streaming entropy engine is characterized rather than asserted: its complexity is stated as expected amortised constant time under named data-structure assumptions, and its floating-point drift is measured over 12 million updates and converted into the number of classifier decisions it changes, which is zero. The explanation trigger is defined as a numbered condition including a budget term, and we measure the throughput collapse that attributing every positive prediction causes and the throughput three mitigations recover, producing a coverage-versus-throughput frontier an operator can select from. The control-plane cost is measured inside a running controller rather than extrapolated from offline inference, including the rate at which a single controller saturates and the flow-rule aggregation needed to keep a bounded TCAM from overflowing. To our knowledge no prior SDN DDoS detector reports the second or third of these. We also now state plainly what we do not claim, including that the entropy augmentation does not improve in-distribution accuracy on this corpus.
R7.1.action: Rewrote the contributions as four measurable claims, added a positioning table with the axes on which the work differs, and added an explicit non-dominance statement.
